one_sentence: All substantive fields (author, title, year, volume, pages, ISSN) check out against CrossRef/RePEc for Lutz (2015, J. Banking & Finance, vol. 61, pp. 89-105, DOI 10.1016/j.jbankfin.2015.08.019) — issues are purely BibTeX hygiene from an uncleaned WoS export.

issues.original:
The impact of conventional and unconventional monetary policy on
   investor sentiment
issues.corrected: The impact of conventional and unconventional monetary policy on investor sentiment
issues.reason: WoS export line-wrapped the title across two physical lines with a hanging indent; content is correct, just needs reflow to a single line. Matches CrossRef title exactly (case-preserved, no other change needed).
WoS exports journal names in ALL-CAPS; canonical title-case form per CrossRef/publisher is 'Journal of Banking & Finance'. The '\&' escaping for BibTeX/LaTeX is correct and should be kept.

issues.corrected: (absent — confirmed correct, no issue number needed)
issues.reason: CrossRef records this article's issue as 'C' (Elsevier's placeholder for continuous/no-issue numbering), i.e. Journal of Banking & Finance volume 61 was published without discrete issue numbers. The missing 'Number' field in the entry is therefore not an error and should NOT be added.
DOI absent from the WoS export; confirmed via CrossRef lookup (container-title, volume, pages, ISSN all match). Should be added as a Doi field.
Web of Science internal accession number, not a standard BibTeX field and meaningless outside WoS; stray artifact of the export. Should be dropped.

issues.corrected: 1872-6372 (value correct, but not a standard BibTeX field)
issues.reason: Not a standard BibTeX field (BibTeX has no canonical EISSN key); most styles only use ISSN. The value itself is verified correct (JBF's e-ISSN per Elsevier/library records) but the field is redundant WoS-export baggage — safe to drop or fold into a note, not required for citation correctness.

Minor hygiene: WoS exports the month code in caps; standard BibTeX convention uses the lowercase three-letter macro (dec), which resolves to December — matches CrossRef's 2015-12 publication date, so no factual change, just casing/style.
